title: Airline dispatch reroute notice
description: An airline operations control notice that a flight is rerouted because of space weather: HF radio blackout or radiation on a polar or high-latitude route, or GNSS degradation. States the flight, the original and new routes, the reason with the level in NOAA scale terms, the communications plan when HF is lost, the effect on time and fuel, and the dispatcher. No radiation dose figures; the decision and its basis only.

examples: Polar route over the Arctic Ocean
Southern Pacific track via the Aleutians

reason.description: Why, with the NOAA scale level and the source product.
examples: S3 (Strong) radiation storm in progress per SWPC alert and HF radio unreliable on the polar track.
Position reports by satellite voice and data link; HF is backup only.
Adds 55 minutes and 3,900 kg of fuel; the fuel load has been adjusted.
Exercise notice. The airline and flight are fictional.
